sections.heading: C - California Driver's Handbook Section Four: Changing, Replacing, Renewing
sections.markdown:
## C - California Driver's Handbook Section Four: Changing, Replacing, Renewing

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Legal name changes and license updates such as physical description or gender identity are handled at dmv.ca.gov/dlservices [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Movers must tell DMV their new address within ten days [A01].
Why it matters: the ten-day report clock is the headline rule of this section.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Address changes go in online at dmv.ca.gov/addresschange or by mail, and keeping the mailing address current stays the driver's own responsibility [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
A new address never triggers an automatic new license, though a replacement can be requested for a fee [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Driving while the license is expired breaks the law [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Lost, stolen, or damaged licenses are renewed or replaced through dmv.ca.gov/dlservices, or at a DMV office when online renewal is unavailable [A01].
Why it matters: the office visit is the fallback branch, not the default path.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
DMV may demand extra identity proof before issuing, and a license sharing its expiry date with the identity document forces you to supply a valid identity document [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Minor applicants need a parent or guardian signature on the application [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
The old card dies the moment the replacement arrives, so destroy it if it turns up [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
Out-of-state drivers who cannot renew may seek a one-year extension before expiry by emailing name, license number, birth date, California residence address, and out-of-state address to dl-extensions@dmv.ca.gov [A01].
Why it matters: the five-item email packet is the most-missed list in this section.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
Limited-term licenses are barred from that extension [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
